ON BY DEFAULT

Current, without
interrupting your work.

ShellGuardian checks for its own updates at launch and every six hours while open. Signed updates download in the background and install when you close the app normally.

Prefer to choose? Turn automatic updates off in settings. Your choice is saved in one small preference file. No database, update daemon, or browser storage.

OpenShell updates are separate. We show its installed version and release status, but never upgrade your runtime automatically.

A few useful boundaries.

Does ShellGuardian replace OpenShell?

No. OpenShell owns credentials, authentication, agent state, policy enforcement, and sandbox isolation. ShellGuardian delegates through your installed CLI and registered gateways. It is an independent project, not an NVIDIA product.

Can I track inference tokens or credential usage?

Not yet. The inspected OpenShell 0.1.2 CLI does not expose token totals, credential-use counters, or CPU/memory usage. ShellGuardian marks those as unavailable, never as zero. Provider attachments describe access, not evidence that a credential was used.

What stays on my computer?

Your existing OpenShell configuration stays where it is. ShellGuardian adds an executable, launcher, desktop entry, and at most one update-preference file. It does not add a database, copy secrets, or archive agent activity.

How ready is the app?

This is an early Linux preview. CLI contracts and browser flows are tested, but live policy/provider/lifecycle mutation and physical remote-host acceptance are still open. Use a disposable test environment before trusting new controls in an important workflow. See acceptance evidence.
